problems.claim: Episode visitation induction implies an optimal single-episode policy without defining a mixture.
problems.evidence: Exact two-terminal example: episode marginals (.9,.1) and (.1,.9); each has coverage .098137..., whereas uniform mixture .255.
problems.alternative_explanation: The intended output is likely normalized cumulative occupancy or a uniformly selected episode.
problems.dependency: Only the theorem-to-objective identification; cumulative balancing induction remains valid.
problems.repair: Explicit uniform episode mixture or cumulative objective; no retraining required for this mathematical repair.

independent_verification.source_claim: Read physical p4 Objective4.1 expected one-trajectory feature matrix, p5 Proposition4.2, and full pp15-16 PropositionA.1 proof. Source explicitly considers n_beta interaction rounds and concludes uniform terminal-feature probability after those rounds; it does not explicitly select an output episode.
independent_verification.assumptions_verified: Deterministic one-step transition, finite two actions, common initial state, terminal-only one-hot features, n_beta=2 and behavior(.9,.1), with0<epsilon<.1. Both terminal directions retained. First-round coverage event is tied and has probability1; second round selects the previously unvisited state with positive behavior support.

decisive_check.argument: The conditional algorithm visits both directions exactly once on every two-round run, so (1/2)sum_t E[e_terminal_t e_terminal_t^T]=I/2. Neither individual marginal equalsI/2. Convexity of reciprocal with fixed total mass proves mixture optimality.

independent_verification.counterevidence: The source explicitly discusses cumulative interaction and says after n_beta episodes. Thus a uniform-episode/empirical-occupancy interpretation is plausible and the counterexample does not refute that intended cumulative statement. It does refute reading the final probability as that of each episode or the last episode.
independent_verification.core_dependency: This is the link between the ideal conditioning proposition and Objective4.1. No theorem guarantees approximate diffusion policies in the continuous-feature experiments, and no such guarantee is inferred. The proof establishes cumulative balancing under its restrictive assumptions.
independent_verification.severity_and_repair: Retain Minor as an output-policy specification ambiguity, not because the repair is easy or experiments survive. The source does not unambiguously promise uniformity for a named last episode; hence a disproved literal per-episode interpretation cannot by itself establish a false intended core theorem. State uniform random episode with its induced histories, or redefine normalized cumulative objective. Do not certify original per-episode optimality. Intermediate w(s) notation needs time-indexed reachability, without changing the support argument.
